standard_prerequisites.name: A maximal subfield splits the algebra
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a finite central skew field is split by a maximal subfield, which turns the second assertion of the statement into the first.

standard_prerequisites.name: The centralizer of a separable subfield
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the discussion of centralizers of subfields of a central skew field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the centralizer of a separable subfield again has that subfield as its center, which is what allows the author to replace the ground field and reduce to finding one separable element.

standard_prerequisites.name: Inseparable elements and minimal polynomials
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that in positive characteristic an element whose minimal polynomial is not separable has a minimal polynomial of the form a p-power variable minus a constant.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change and the algebraic closure case
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma lemma-base-change and Lemma lemma-brauer-algebraically-closed
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply that extending scalars to the algebraic closure turns the skew field into a matrix algebra, which produces the element whose p-th power is not central.

core_obligations: Reduction to one separable element (proof lines 931-953): since every Brauer class is represented by a finite central skew field, the second assertion follows from the first; then the author observes that if a separable subfield is given, the centralizer of it has that subfield as center, so the problem reduces to showing that whenever the ground field is not all of the skew field there is a separable element outside it, and he disposes of characteristic zero and of finite ground fields.

The contradiction setup (proof lines 954-962): assuming no element is separable over an infinite field of positive characteristic, the cited discussion of inseparable elements shows that every minimal polynomial has the form of a p-power variable minus a constant, and since the degrees are bounded by the dimension one fixed p-power q satisfies that the q-th power of every element of the skew field lies in the ground field.

The polynomial map (proof lines 964-972): writing the q-th power map in terms of a basis, each coordinate is a polynomial in the coordinates of the element, a fact the author states with the parenthetical that the details are omitted, and the choice of q together with infiniteness of the ground field makes all but the first of these polynomials identically zero.

The contradiction (proof lines 972-977): those polynomials remain zero after extending scalars to the algebraic closure, where the algebra becomes a matrix algebra, and in a matrix algebra there are elements, such as a matrix unit, whose q-th power is not central; this contradicts the conclusion of the previous step.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the class statement to the subfield statement using the splitting lemma.
Reduce to finding one element separable over the ground field.
Assume the contrary in positive characteristic and extract a fixed p-power whose map lands in the ground field.
Write that map in coordinates, use infiniteness to kill the coordinates above the first, and contradict a computation in a matrix algebra after extending scalars.
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that a finite central skew field over a field contains a maximal subfield separable over the ground field, and hence that every Brauer class has a finite separable splitting field (statement lines 922-929). The proof is a complete argument: the class statement is reduced to the subfield statement by a named lemma, and the subfield statement is reduced to the existence of one separable element outside the ground field by passing to a centralizer (proof lines 931-953); assuming the contrary in positive characteristic, the author extracts a fixed p-power whose map sends the skew field into the ground field (proof lines 954-962), expresses that map in coordinates of a chosen basis and kills all coordinates above the first using the infinitude of the ground field (proof lines 964-972); extending scalars to the algebraic closure makes the algebra a matrix algebra in which a matrix unit has noncentral p-th power, giving the contradiction (proof lines 972-977). The non-formal content is the coordinate argument and the final matrix computation. The claim is H3.
